records.source: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος, οὐκ ἀπ’ ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ δι’ ἀνθρώπου ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ πάντες ἀδελφοί, ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας·
records.gloss: Paul, apostle, not from men nor through man but through Jesus Christ and God Father the [one] having raised him out of [the] dead, \v 2 and the with me all brothers, to the churches of the Galatia:
pieces: From Paul, an apostle sent not from any human source, nor through any human go-between, but through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and God the Father, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead,
and from all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who are with me, to the churches of Galatia.

L.1: Paul, an apostle, not from human beings nor through a human being, but through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and God [the] Father, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from [the] dead,
L.2: and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} with me, to the churches of Galatia:

R.1: This letter is from Paul, an apostle. No human group sent me out, and no person made me an apostle. Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and God the Father sent me. It was God who raised Jesus from the dead.
R.2: All the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who are here with me join me in writing to the churches in Galatia.

decisions.choice: not from human beings nor through a human being: no human source and no human go-between stands behind Paul's apostleship
alternatives: two ways of saying the same thing, with no difference between the phrases
decisions.reason: ἀπ names where something comes from, δι the one through whom it comes. Paul denies both: his commission did not start with any human authority, and no single person handed it on to him. The singular in the second phrase may answer a claim that some leader, perhaps in Jerusalem, had made him an apostle; 1:11-24 answers that claim at length.

decisions.choice: human beings in general, not men as distinct from women
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος is the ordinary word for a human being. The contrast here is between human and divine, not between men and women.

decisions.choice: Jesus Christ and God the Father together are the source of Paul's commission, and God is named as the one who raised Jesus
decisions.reason: One διὰ governs both names, so Paul places Jesus Christ beside God the Father as the one who sent him. He adds that the Father raised Jesus from the dead: Paul's commission came from the risen Christ (1:16; 1 Corinthians 9:1; 15:8), not from the apostles who had known Jesus before.

decisions.choice: the churches of Galatia: several congregations in the Roman province of Galatia, in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey)
alternatives: the churches in the old territory of the Galatian people in the north of the province
the churches of the southern part of the province (Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe, Acts 13-14)
decisions.reason: The letter is addressed to a group of churches, not one city. Galatia was both the name of a people settled in the north of the region and of a larger Roman province reaching further south, and which churches Paul means cannot be settled from the letter itself. The translation is the same either way.

decisions.choice: all the brothers and sisters with me: the believers who were with Paul as he wrote, joining in the greeting
decisions.reason: Paul names no fellow sender, as he does in Philippians 1:1 and Colossians 1:1, but includes everyone with him. ἀδελφοί is masculine plural, the ordinary way to speak of a group of men and women together.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Title and gender settings, as Colossians 1:1-2 has them.

decisions.choice: raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting for Jesus.

decisions.choice: human beings; any human source; any human go-between (B); no human group, no person (R)
decisions.reason: The word means people of either sex; "men" would suggest males.

decisions.choice: This letter is from Paul ... All the brothers and sisters who are here with me join me in writing to the churches in Galatia.
alternatives: Paul, an apostle ... and all the brothers with me, to the churches of Galatia
decisions.reason: Readable turns the address into ordinary sentences, as Colossians 1:1 does, says plainly who sent Paul, and names the subject of "raised" (God) and its object (Jesus) instead of a pronoun.

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ δόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
records.gloss: grace to you and peace from God Father and Lord of us Jesus Christ, \v 4 the [one] having given himself for the sins of us so that he might deliver us out of the age the present evil according to the will of the God and Father of us, \v 5 to whom the glory to the ages of the ages; amen.
pieces: Grace and peace to you from God the Father and our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}},
who gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, as our God and Father willed.
To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

L.3: Grace to you and peace from God [the] Father and our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.4: who gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} for our sins so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might rescue us out of the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
L.5: to whom [be] the glory to the ages of the ages. Amen.

R.3: May God our Father and our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} show you grace and give you peace.
R.4: Jesus gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to die for our sins. He did it to rescue us from the evil age we live in now. This was what our God and Father wanted.
R.5: May God receive glory forever and ever! Amen.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ"
alternatives: "from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ over where ἡμῶν ("our") stands: after "Lord", as SBLGNT has it, or after "Father", as in Paul's usual greeting (Philippians 1:2). Both are well attested. Either way grace and peace come from the Father and from Jesus Christ, and the meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: who gave himself for our sins: Jesus gave up his life to deal with our sins
alternatives: gave himself up to suffering in general
decisions.reason: "Gave himself" means he gave his life, as in 2:20 ("who loved me and gave himself for me"). ὑπὲρ with "sins" means on account of them, to take them away, as in 1 Corinthians 15:3 ("Christ died for our sins"). Paul puts the cross at the front of the letter before he says anything else.

decisions.choice: the present evil age: the present time of the world, in which evil holds sway, set against the age to come
decisions.reason: αἰών is an age, a period of history. Jewish teaching spoke of "this age" and "the age to come"; Paul says Christ's death already sets believers free from the hold of the present age, though they still live in it (6:14-15 speaks of a new creation). It is not the created world that is evil, but the age under the power of sin.

decisions.choice: according to the will of our God and Father: Christ's self-giving and the rescue it brings were what the Father willed
alternatives: the phrase goes only with "rescue us"
decisions.reason: The phrase closes the whole clause: Christ's giving himself and its purpose both carry out the Father's plan. The Son acts with the Father, not against him.

decisions.choice: to whom: to God the Father, to whom glory belongs for ever
decisions.reason: ᾧ looks back to the nearest name, "our God and Father". The verb is left out, as is usual in such praise: "[be]" or "[is]". The repeated "ages of the ages" is a Hebrew way of saying "for ever".

decisions.choice: Amen: a Hebrew word of agreement, "so be it"
decisions.reason: ἀμήν is a Hebrew word carried into Greek unchanged. A congregation hearing the letter read would answer the praise with it.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Title and pronoun settings.

decisions.choice: age
decisions.reason: "Age" keeps the sense of a period of time and the contrast with the age to come; "world" would suggest the created world, and is kept in this translation for a different Greek word.

decisions.choice: Jesus gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to die for our sins
alternatives: who gave himself for our sins
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus gave himself up to death, which is what "gave himself" means here (2:20).

decisions.choice: May God our Father and our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} show you grace and give you peace. ... May God receive glory forever and ever!
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting and the praise into prayers, as Colossians 1:2 does, and names God instead of "to whom".

decisions.choice: to the ages of the ages (L); for ever and ever (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style phrase; Balanced uses the English phrase with the same force.

records.source: Θαυμάζω ὅτι οὕτως ταχέως μετατίθεσθε ἀπὸ τοῦ καλέσαντος ὑμᾶς ἐν χάριτι Χριστοῦ εἰς ἕτερον εὐαγγέλιον, ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλο· εἰ μή τινές εἰσιν οἱ ταράσσοντες ὑμᾶς καὶ θέλοντες μεταστρέψαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: I am astonished that so quickly you are deserting from the [one] having called you in [the] grace of Christ to a different gospel, \v 7 which not is another; except some are the [ones] troubling you and wanting to distort the gospel of the Christ.
pieces: I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from God, who called you by the grace of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and going over to a different gospel.
But there is no second gospel. There are only some people who are unsettling you and want to twist the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} into something else.

L.6: I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from the one who called you in [the] grace of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to a different gospel,
L.7: which is not another [gospel]; except that there are some who are troubling you and want to distort the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.6: I am shocked that you are so quickly turning away from God. He called you through the grace of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. But now you are turning to a different kind of good news.
R.7: Really, there is no other good news. But some people are confusing you. They want to change the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} into something else.

decisions.choice: Paul goes straight from the greeting to his astonishment, with no thanksgiving
decisions.reason: In his other letters Paul thanks God for the readers after the greeting (Philippians 1:3; Colossians 1:3). Here the thanksgiving is missing, and the first word after the greeting is a rebuke. The letter's hearers would notice the gap.

decisions.choice: the one who called you is God
decisions.reason: Paul regularly speaks of God as the one who calls (1:15; 5:8; Romans 8:30). The participle καλέσαντος stands without a name, but the same verb in 1:15 has God as its subject.

decisions.choice: in the grace of Christ: God called them by means of Christ's grace, and into it
alternatives: called you into the grace of Christ (the place they were called to)
called you in grace (no reference to how)
decisions.reason: ἐν can mark the means ("by") or the sphere ("in"). The two belong together here: the grace Christ gives is both how they were called and what they were called to share. The levels keep "in" or "by" without narrowing it further.

decisions.choice: turning away: deserting one side for another, and still in progress
alternatives: being moved by others (a true passive)
decisions.reason: μετατίθημι was used of soldiers or officials who changed sides. The present tense shows that the desertion is happening as Paul writes and is not yet complete; the letter is written to stop it. The form could be passive ("you are being moved"), but Paul holds the Galatians responsible (3:1-3).

decisions.choice: a different gospel, which is not another gospel: the message they are turning to differs in kind and is no gospel at all
alternatives: a sharp distinction between two Greek words for "other" is meant
decisions.reason: Paul calls it a ἕτερον gospel and at once denies that there is any ἄλλο: he grants it the name only to take it back. The point does not rest on a fixed difference between the two words, which overlap in meaning, but on the denial. There is only one gospel (1:8-9).

decisions.choice: except that: the only thing there is besides the gospel is people unsettling you and trying to twist it
decisions.reason: εἰ μή ("except") qualifies the denial: there is no other gospel; there are only people who trouble the Galatians. ταράσσοντες is the word Paul uses of these teachers again in 5:10, and μεταστρέψαι means to turn something into its opposite.

decisions.choice: grace of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article the Greek has before the second title.

decisions.choice: God, who called you (B); turning away from God. He called you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, the one Paul means (m2), since "the one who called you" leaves many readers unsure.

decisions.choice: twist ... into something else (B); change ... into something else (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn something into something different; "pervert" now has other associations in English.

decisions.choice: a different kind of good news
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the difference is one of kind (m5).

records.heading: There is no other gospel

records.source: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐὰν ἡμεῖς ἢ ἄγγελος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ εὐαγγελίζηται ὑμῖν παρ’ ὃ εὐηγγελισάμεθα ὑμῖν, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
records.gloss: But even if we or an angel out of heaven should preach-the-gospel to you contrary to what we preached-the-gospel to you, accursed let him be.
pieces: But even if we ourselves, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let that one be under God's curse.

L.8: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel to you contrary to what we preached to you, let that one be accursed.

R.8: But suppose we ourselves, or even an angel from heaven, told you good news that is different from the good news we told you. Then may God's curse fall on them!

decisions.choice: even if: a case Paul does not expect, put as strongly as possible
decisions.reason: ἐὰν with the subjunctive sets out a supposition. Paul names the most trustworthy messengers he can think of, himself and his companions or an angel from heaven, to show that the message matters more than the messenger.

decisions.choice: contrary to: any gospel other than the one Paul preached, which by being other opposes it
alternatives: in addition to (adding something to Paul's gospel)
decisions.reason: παρ with the accusative can mean "against" or "beside, beyond". In Galatians the two come to the same thing: the teachers wanted to add circumcision and the law to the gospel (5:2-4), and that addition changed it into another message.

decisions.choice: accursed: placed under God's curse, handed over to his judgment
alternatives: excluded from the church (church discipline only)
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament ἀνάθεμα is something devoted to God for destruction (Leviticus 27:28-29; Joshua 6:17). Paul uses it for being cut off from Christ (Romans 9:3; 1 Corinthians 16:22). The curse is in God's hands; Paul is not calling on the church to carry it out.

decisions.choice: let that one be accursed (L); let that one be under God's curse (B); may God's curse fall on them (R)
decisions.reason: "Anathema" is not current English. Balanced and Readable say whose curse it is (m3) without deciding more than the word says.

decisions.choice: that one; them
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject, and Paul includes himself, his companions and any messenger; "that one" and "them" do not limit it to a man.

decisions.choice: But suppose ... Then may God's curse fall on them!
alternatives: But even if we or an angel from heaven ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition and the curse into two sentences.

records.source: ὡς προειρήκαμεν, καὶ ἄρτι πάλιν λέγω, εἴ τις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρ’ ὃ παρελάβετε, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
records.gloss: As we have said before, and now again I say, if anyone you preaches-a-gospel contrary to what you received, accursed let him be.
pieces: We have said it before, and now I say it again: if anyone preaches to you a gospel other than the one you received, let that one be under God's curse.

L.9: As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone is preaching a gospel to you contrary to what you received, let that one be accursed.

R.9: We told you this before, and now I am telling you again. If anyone tells you good news that is different from the good news you accepted, may God's curse fall on them!

decisions.choice: as we have said before: most likely when Paul was with them, though it may point back to verse 8
decisions.reason: προειρήκαμεν is a perfect, "we have said before", and Paul sets it against "now again I say". That contrast fits a warning given during his earlier visit better than one written a sentence ago. The words keep both readings open.

decisions.choice: if anyone is preaching: no longer a supposition but what is actually happening
decisions.reason: Verse 8 used ἐὰν with the subjunctive ("if ... should"); verse 9 uses εἴ with the indicative, stating a real case: someone is preaching another gospel to the Galatians now.

decisions.choice: received: took over a message handed on to them, as a tradition is received
decisions.reason: παραλαμβάνω is the word Paul uses for receiving the gospel as something passed on (1 Corinthians 15:1-3). It turns the warning toward the Galatians: the gospel is the one they themselves accepted.

decisions.choice: let that one be accursed (L); let that one be under God's curse (B); may God's curse fall on them (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: tells you good news
decisions.reason: Readable uses "tell the good news" for the verb throughout Galatians.

records.source: Ἄρτι γὰρ ἀνθρώπους πείθω ἢ τὸν θεόν;
records.gloss: Now for men am I persuading, or the God?
pieces: Is it people I am trying to win over now, or God?

L.10: For am I now winning over human beings, or God?

R.10: So, am I now trying to win people over? Or am I trying to win God's approval?

decisions.choice: trying to win over: seeking someone's favor
decisions.reason: πείθω here means to try to win someone over. No one argues God round, so the sense is seeking favor, as the next question ("seeking to please") shows. Paul may be answering a charge that he had made the gospel easy in order to win people (compare 5:11).

decisions.choice: now, after such a curse: these strong words show Paul is not courting anyone's favor
alternatives: "now" contrasts with Paul's life before he met Christ
decisions.reason: γὰρ links the question to the curses just spoken: a man who says that is hardly flattering his hearers. Ἄρτι ("now") points to what he has just written.

decisions.choice: winning over (L); trying to win over (B)
decisions.reason: The present tense describes an attempt; "win over" covers both people and God without suggesting an argument with God.

decisions.choice: Or am I trying to win God's approval?
decisions.reason: Readable writes out the second half of the question.

records.gloss: Or do I seek men to please?
pieces: Or is my aim to please people?

L.10: Or am I seeking to please human beings?

R.10: Is my goal to make people happy with me?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: Paul's second question restates the first in plainer terms. The next sentence gives his answer.

decisions.choice: seeking to please (L); is my aim to please (B); is my goal to make people happy with me (R)
decisions.reason: ζητῶ is "seek"; Balanced and Readable say it as an aim.

records.source: εἰ ἔτι ἀνθρώποις ἤρεσκον, Χριστοῦ δοῦλος οὐκ ἂν ἤμην.
records.gloss: If still men I were pleasing, of Christ slave not would I be.
pieces: If I were still out to please people, I would be no servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.10: If I were still pleasing human beings, I would not be a slave of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.10: If I were still trying to make people happy with me, I would not be a servant who belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: Paul is not pleasing people, and he is Christ's slave
decisions.reason: The past tenses with ἂν state what would be true if the condition were met, implying that it is not.

decisions.choice: still: as Paul once did, before Christ called him
alternatives: simply "any longer", with no reference to his past
decisions.reason: ἔτι implies a time when Paul did seek human approval. Verses 13-14 describe his earlier zeal in Judaism, which won him standing among his people. The word may also be a plain "any longer".

decisions.choice: slave: someone owned by a master and wholly at his service
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1, δοῦλος is a slave. A slave serves one master; a man owned by Christ cannot also make pleasing people his aim.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: Γνωρίζω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον·
records.gloss: I make known for to you, brothers, the gospel the [one] having been preached by me, that not it is according to man;
pieces: For I want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that the gospel I preached is no human invention.

L.11: For I make known to you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, the gospel that was preached by me, that it is not of human [origin];

R.11: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I want you to understand this. The good news I told you is not something people made up.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "for"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts are divided between γὰρ ("for") and a weaker connecting word ("but, now"). With "for", Paul explains why he is no people-pleaser (verse 10); with the other, he simply begins a new section. The statement itself is the same.

decisions.choice: I make known to you: a solemn opening for an important statement
alternatives: I am telling you something new
decisions.reason: Γνωρίζω introduces a statement Paul wants the readers to take to heart (1 Corinthians 15:1; 2 Corinthians 8:1). The Galatians already knew his gospel; he is stating where it came from.

decisions.choice: not human: not of human origin, and so not shaped by human standards
decisions.reason: κατὰ ἄνθρωπον can mean "by human standards" (1 Corinthians 3:3) or "from a human source". Verse 12 explains it in terms of source: Paul did not receive the gospel from any person. Origin is the main point, with its character following from it.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters: the believers of the Galatian churches, men and women
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί is masculine plural, the ordinary way to address a mixed group.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting, as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: of human [origin] (L); no human invention (B); not something people made up (R)
decisions.reason: "According to man" is not clear English. The levels say what the phrase means here (m3).

records.heading: Paul's gospel came from God, not from people

records.source: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου παρέλαβον αὐτό, οὔτε ἐδιδάχθην, ἀλλὰ δι’ ἀποκαλύψεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Not-even for I from man received it, nor was I taught [it], but through revelation of Jesus Christ.
pieces: I did not receive it from any human being, and nobody taught it to me. It came to me through a revelation of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.12: For I did not receive it from a human being, nor was I taught [it], but [I received it] through a revelation of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.12: No person gave it to me, and no one taught it to me. Instead, God showed Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} to me, and that is how I received it.

decisions.choice: received ... taught: Paul did not get the gospel as a tradition handed down or as lessons from a teacher
decisions.reason: παραλαμβάνω is the word for receiving teaching handed on (1:9; 1 Corinthians 15:3), and διδάσκω for learning it from a teacher. Paul does not deny that he later learned facts from others (1:18); he denies that his gospel and its authority came that way.

decisions.choice: a revelation of Jesus Christ: God's unveiling of Jesus Christ to Paul
alternatives: a revelation from Jesus Christ (Jesus is the one who revealed it)
decisions.reason: After ἀποκαλύψεως the name can be what was revealed or who revealed it. Verse 16 says God was pleased "to reveal his Son" to Paul, which favors Jesus Christ as the one revealed. But the risen Jesus also spoke to Paul (Acts 9:4-6), and the other reading is fully possible. Either way the gospel came to Paul straight from heaven, not from people.

decisions.choice: the revelation Paul received when the risen Jesus appeared to him near Damascus
decisions.reason: ἀποκάλυψις is an unveiling of what was hidden. Paul places it just before his return to Damascus (1:15-17); Acts 9 tells the story, and 1 Corinthians 15:8 counts it as an appearance of the risen Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: but [I received it] through
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb the Greek carries over from the first clause.

decisions.choice: Instead, God showed Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} to me, and that is how I received it.
alternatives: but through a revelation of Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable says what the revelation was, following the reading chosen in m2 and verse 16.

records.source: Ἠκούσατε γὰρ τὴν ἐμὴν ἀναστροφήν ποτε ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ, ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ἐδίωκον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐπόρθουν αὐτήν, καὶ προέκοπτον ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ὑπὲρ πολλοὺς συνηλικιώτας ἐν τῷ γένει μου, περισσοτέρως ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τῶν πατρικῶν μου παραδόσεων.
records.gloss: You heard for of the my way-of-life formerly in the Judaism, that beyond measure I was persecuting the church of the God and was destroying it, \v 14 and I was advancing in the Judaism beyond many contemporaries in the race of me, more abundantly zealous being of the ancestral of me traditions.
pieces: You have heard about the way I once lived in Judaism: how fiercely I persecuted God's church and set out to destroy it.
I was moving ahead in Judaism faster than many people my age among my own people, because I was far more zealous for the traditions handed down from my ancestors.

L.13: For you have heard of my way of life formerly in Judaism, that beyond measure I was persecuting the church of God and trying to destroy it,
L.14: and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, being far more zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

R.13: You have heard how I used to live when I was devoted to Judaism, the Jewish way of life. I attacked God's church with great violence. I tried to wipe it out.
R.14: I was going further in Judaism than many others my age among my people. I was much more eager than they were to keep the traditions handed down from my ancestors.

decisions.choice: Judaism: the Jewish way of life, practiced in strict loyalty to the law and the customs of the people
alternatives: a religion separate from faith in Christ, in the modern sense
decisions.reason: Ἰουδαϊσμός is a rare word, used in Jewish writings of the time for holding firmly to Jewish ways against foreign customs (2 Maccabees 2:21; 8:1). Paul does not stop being a Jew (2:15); what he left behind is the zeal of that way of life as the measure of standing with God.

decisions.choice: I kept persecuting the church and was trying to destroy it
decisions.reason: Both verbs are imperfect: they describe something repeated over a time. πορθέω was used of sacking a city; the imperfect shows an attempt that did not succeed, as verse 23 confirms.

decisions.choice: the church of God: God's people gathered in Christ, the whole body Paul attacked
decisions.reason: Paul uses ἐκκλησία for a local congregation (1:2) and for God's people as a whole, as here (1 Corinthians 15:9).

decisions.choice: zealous: fiercely devoted, ready to act against anyone who broke the law
alternatives: a member of the Zealot party
decisions.reason: ζηλωτής recalls Phinehas and Elijah, who acted with violence for God's honor (Numbers 25:11-13; 1 Kings 19:10). Paul's zeal explains his persecution (Philippians 3:6). There is no sign he means the later political party.

decisions.choice: the traditions of my fathers: the teaching handed down among the Pharisees alongside the written law
decisions.reason: Paul was a Pharisee (Philippians 3:5). The Pharisees kept παράδοσις, rules and interpretations passed down from earlier teachers (Mark 7:3-5).

decisions.choice: my contemporaries among my people: Jews of Paul's own age
decisions.reason: συνηλικιώτης means someone of the same age; γένος here is Paul's people, the Jews.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "my fathers"; Balanced and Readable use the plain English word for the generations before.

decisions.choice: Judaism, the Jewish way of life
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word as m1 describes it, so that it is not read as a separate religion.

decisions.choice: fiercely (B); with great violence (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means to an extreme degree; the context is violent persecution.

records.source: ὅτε δὲ εὐδόκησεν ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εὐθέως οὐ προσανεθέμην σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι, οὐδὲ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ ἀποστόλους, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθον εἰς Ἀραβίαν, καὶ πάλιν ὑπέστρεψα εἰς Δαμασκόν.
records.gloss: When but was pleased the [one] having set-apart me from [the] womb of mother of me and having called through the grace of him \v 16 to reveal the son of him in me so that I might preach him among the nations, immediately not I consulted with flesh and blood, \v 17 nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the before me apostles, but I went away into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.
pieces: But God set me apart from birth and called me by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose
to reveal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son in me so that I would proclaim the gospel about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the Gentiles, I did not at once turn to any human being for advice.
I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead I went away to Arabia, and afterward I came back to Damascus.

L.15: But when the one who set me apart from my mother's womb and called [me] through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace was pleased
L.16: to reveal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son in me, so that I might preach {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the Gentiles, immediately I did not consult with flesh and blood,
L.17: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those [who were] apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.

R.15: But even before I was born, God set me apart. Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called me. Then the time came when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was pleased
R.16: to show me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, so that I would tell the good news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to people who are not Jews. When that happened, I did not go to any person for advice.
R.17: I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went off to Arabia. Later I went back to the city of Damascus.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the one who set me apart", without the word "God"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "God" after εὐδόκησεν; some important early ones do not, and SBLGNT follows them. A copyist was more likely to add the name than to drop it. The meaning is the same: the one who set Paul apart is God.

decisions.choice: set apart from his mother's womb and called: Paul's call is told in words used of the prophets
decisions.reason: The wording recalls Jeremiah 1:5 ("before you came out of the womb I set you apart ... a prophet to the nations") and Isaiah 49:1-6 (the servant called from the womb to be a light to the nations). Like them, Paul was chosen before birth and sent to the nations.

decisions.choice: in me: God revealed his Son to Paul, within him, so that Paul came to know him
alternatives: through me (God showed his Son to others through Paul's life)
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐμοὶ most naturally means God's inward revealing of Christ to Paul, the same event as "a revelation of Jesus Christ" in verse 12. It could also mean God revealed Christ through Paul to others, which the purpose clause ("so that I might preach him") would suit.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the non-Jewish peoples
decisions.reason: ἔθνος in the plural is Paul's word for the peoples other than Israel (2:7-9).

decisions.choice: flesh and blood: any human being
decisions.reason: σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι is a Jewish expression for human beings in their weakness compared with God (Matthew 16:17). εὐθέως ("immediately") goes with the whole sentence: Paul's first move was not to consult anyone, but to go to Arabia.

decisions.choice: Arabia: the Nabatean kingdom to the south and east of Damascus; Damascus: the city where Paul first met the risen Christ
decisions.reason: Paul does not say what he did in Arabia. "Returned to Damascus" shows he had been there before going; Acts 9:1-22 places his conversion near the city.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting for God and his Son.

decisions.choice: God
alternatives: the one who set me apart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, whom the phrase means (m1).

decisions.choice: from birth (B); even before I was born (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means from the start of his life; Readable follows Jeremiah 1:5, which it recalls (m2).

decisions.choice: I did not at once turn to any human being for advice (B); I did not go to any person for advice (R)
alternatives: I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood
decisions.reason: "Flesh and blood" is kept at Literal; the other levels say what it means (m5).

decisions.choice: proclaim the gospel about him (B); tell the good news about him (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "proclaim as good news"; Balanced and Readable say what Paul proclaims.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles" (m4).

records.source: Ἔπειτα μετὰ ἔτη τρία ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἱστορῆσαι Κηφᾶν, καὶ ἐπέμεινα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας δεκαπέντε·
records.gloss: Then after years three I went up to Jerusalem to get-to-know Cephas, and I remained with him days fifteen;
pieces: Three years later I did go up to Jerusalem, to get to know Cephas, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.

L.18: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Cephas, and I remained with him fifteen days.

R.18: Three years after that, I did go up to Jerusalem. I went to get to know Peter, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.

decisions.choice: after three years: counted most likely from Paul's call (verses 15-16)
alternatives: counted from his return to Damascus
decisions.reason: Ἔπειτα ("then") marks the next step in Paul's account, and the starting point is most naturally the event the account began with. Ancient counting often included the first and last years, so the time may have been a little over two years.

decisions.choice: to get to know Cephas: a visit to meet him and learn from him in person
alternatives: to be taught the gospel by him
decisions.reason: ἱστορέω was used of visiting a person or place in order to come to know it. It implies more than a courtesy call, but Paul's point (verses 11-12) is that this short visit, years after his call, was not where his gospel came from.

decisions.choice: Cephas: the apostle Peter
decisions.reason: Κηφᾶς is the Aramaic word for "rock", the name Jesus gave Simon (John 1:42). Peter is the Greek form of the same name, which Paul uses in 2:7-8.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Readable uses the name readers know (m3). Literal and Balanced keep the name Paul uses.

records.heading: Paul's first visit to Jerusalem

records.source: ἕτερον δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: Other but of the apostles not I saw, except James the brother of the Lord.
pieces: Apart from James, the Lord's brother, I did not see any of the other apostles.

L.19: But I did not see another of the apostles, except James the brother of the Lord.

R.19: I did not see any of the other apostles. The only one I saw was James, the brother of the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: except James: James is counted among the apostles, in a wider sense than the Twelve
alternatives: I saw no other apostle, only James (who was not an apostle)
decisions.reason: εἰ μὴ can mean "except" (James is one of the apostles) or "but only" (James is outside the group). Paul lists James among those to whom the risen Jesus appeared, followed by "all the apostles" (1 Corinthians 15:7), and names him with Cephas and John as a pillar of the church (2:9).

decisions.choice: James the brother of the Lord: Jesus' brother, a leader of the church in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names a James among Jesus' brothers. This is not James the son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve, who was put to death early (Acts 12:2), but the James who led the Jerusalem church (2:9, 12; Acts 15:13). Christian traditions differ on whether these brothers were later sons of Mary or relatives in a wider sense; Paul's word is the ordinary word for brother.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus as the Lord meant.

records.source: ἃ δὲ γράφω ὑμῖν, ἰδοὺ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.
records.gloss: What but I write to you, look, before the God, that not I lie.
pieces: Now, as God sees me, I am not lying in what I write to you.

L.20: Now [in] what I am writing to you, look, before God, I am not lying.

R.20: God knows that what I am writing to you is true. I am not lying!

decisions.choice: before God I am not lying: an oath calling God as witness
decisions.reason: Paul swears to the truth of his account in the same way in Romans 9:1 and 2 Corinthians 11:31. The sentence is incomplete in Greek ("look, before God, that I am not lying"): a verb such as "I declare" is understood before ὅτι.

decisions.choice: what I am writing to you: the account of Paul's movements in verses 15-19
decisions.reason: The oath stands in the middle of the account and backs up the facts just given, which the teachers in Galatia seem to have told differently.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: Modern English, as the style guide asks.

decisions.choice: as God sees me (B); God knows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the call on God means instead of reproducing the exclamation.

records.source: ἔπειτα ἦλθον εἰς τὰ κλίματα τῆς Συρίας καὶ τῆς Κιλικίας.
records.gloss: Then I went into the regions of the Syria and of the Cilicia.
pieces: After that I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

L.21: Then I went into the regions of Syria and of Cilicia.

R.21: After that I went to the areas of Syria and Cilicia.

decisions.choice: Syria and Cilicia: the region around Antioch and, to its northwest, the coastland around Tarsus, Paul's home city
decisions.reason: Syria and Cilicia were joined in one Roman province at the time. Acts 9:30 says Paul was sent to Tarsus, and Acts 11:25-26 that he later worked in Antioch. Both are far from Judea, which is Paul's point (verse 22).

decisions.choice: areas
decisions.reason: A plainer word.

records.source: ἤμην δὲ ἀγνοούμενος τῷ προσώπῳ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Ἰουδαίας ταῖς ἐν Χριστῷ, μόνον δὲ ἀκούοντες ἦσαν ὅτι Ὁ διώκων ἡμᾶς ποτε νῦν εὐαγγελίζεται τὴν πίστιν ἥν ποτε ἐπόρθει, καὶ ἐδόξαζον ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν θεόν.
records.gloss: I was but being-unknown by the face to the churches of the Judea the [ones] in Christ, \v 23 only but hearing they were that "The [one] persecuting us formerly now preaches the faith which formerly he was destroying," \v 24 and they were glorifying in me the God.
pieces: The churches of Judea that are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} still did not know me by sight.
They only kept hearing it said, "The man who used to persecute us is now proclaiming the faith he once set out to destroy."
And because of me they glorified God.

L.22: But I remained unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}};
L.23: they were only hearing, "The one who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith that he once tried to destroy,"
L.24: and they glorified God because of me.

R.22: At that time the churches in Judea that belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} had never met me.
R.23: All they knew was what others were saying: "The man who used to attack us is now telling others the good news, the very faith he once tried to wipe out!"
R.24: And they gave glory to God because of what had happened to me.

decisions.choice: I remained unknown ... they kept hearing: a state that lasted through those years
decisions.reason: Both verbs are formed with εἰμί and a participle, which describes a continuing state: Paul stayed a stranger to them, and all they had was a report that kept reaching them.

decisions.choice: unknown by face to the churches of Judea: the believers in Judea had not met Paul in person
decisions.reason: τῷ προσώπῳ means "by sight". Judea here is the wider region; Paul had spent fifteen days in Jerusalem, mainly with Cephas (verses 18-19), and was not known to the congregations at large.

decisions.choice: in Christ: the Judean congregations that belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase marks these as Christian churches, as distinct from the Jewish synagogues of Judea.

decisions.choice: the faith: the message believed, the gospel that calls for faith
alternatives: trust in Christ (the act of believing)
decisions.reason: Paul uses πίστις here for the content of what is believed, almost a name for the gospel itself, since it can be preached and attacked. Elsewhere in Galatians the word is usually the act of trusting (2:16).

decisions.choice: because of me: they praised God for what he had done in Paul
alternatives: in me (God was seen at work in Paul)
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐμοὶ gives the reason for the praise: the change in Paul, the persecutor turned preacher.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: is now preaching the faith (L); is now proclaiming the faith (B); is now telling others the good news, the very faith (R)
alternatives: preaches the gospel of the faith
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for proclaiming the gospel; its object here is "the faith" (m4), so Literal and Balanced use "preach" and "proclaim", and Readable keeps "tell the good news" and adds "the faith" beside it.

decisions.choice: had never met me
alternatives: were unknown to me by face
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: because of what had happened to me
decisions.reason: Readable says why they praised God (m5).
